After finishing my school days I taught two years and then went back to my first love—printer's ink—and secured a position in a printing office where I was foreman of the Van Alstyne News; then, in August, 1892, I established the Van Alstyne Leader and presently took in a partner, Mr. W. E. Donnan, who was a chemistry student at Grayson College and subsequently became a teacher in the Chemistry Department of the State University. In 1897 we sold the Leader to R. S. Fulton (who still owns it being 81). Then for a short time I was advertising solicitor and manager of the Sherman Daily Register. That year we started as the W. P. Forest. We incorporated the Reynolds-Parker Company as a stock company for commercial printing. For some years I was the manager of the office here, and in 1907 established The Office Supply Store, which I ran for ten years. From 1920 to 1923 I was linotype man on a Tribune, and since 1923 I have managed the Guar-anty Printing Company in Dallas.

In personal matters, I married Miss Dora Lee Johnson, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. J. W. Johnson of Van Alstyne, Texas. We were married on April 4, 1895, and both were born to us; Harold Johnson was born July 30, 1900. After thirty years of poor health and long suffering, Dora died in 1924. I married to Miss Fannie Mae Ball, daughter of the Reverend and Mrs. S. A. Ball, an old and well-to-do family in Mississippi, on December 29, 1925. A son, Leon Ball, born April 21, 1921, and adopted by us when he was four years of age.

In Van Alstyne in August, 1892, I joined the Methodist Church, and in all the succeeding years have been active in church affairs. I was Sunday School Lay Leader, as Bible-class Teacher and Sunday School Superintendent, and for two years was president of Epworth League. In civic life I was for two years an alderman and one year a member of the Citizens Water and Light Committee in Van Alstyne; I have for two two years, president of the Retail Merchants Association one year, on the Board of Trade for two years, and secretary of Rotary as long as I held my membership.
